profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and AI computing company, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA and reported revenue of approximately $215.9 billion for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. The company builds hardware, software, and AI platforms spanning edge to cloud deployment.

On the AI software side, NVIDIA offers the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as designed for long-running, self-evolving agents capable of reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech processing, and safety tasks. Nemotron models are published with open weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license that permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without attribution. The site highlights specific components including Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized task completion, NeMo Switchyard for routing between models, Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding and embedding generation. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site in connection with the vision behind Nemotron. The company also offers NVIDIA NIM, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments, available through build.nvidia.com under an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license.

The held facts record no litigation and no MCP server presence for NVIDIA. The company holds CIK 0001045810 with the SEC and has a verified profile on theworldofai.org as of August 24, 2026.
